title: See how parser choice changes the recovered tree
description: Hold one malformed HTML fragment constant, then change the downstream contract and parser. The tree, serialized output, and contract verdict update together.

parsers.label: html.parser
parsers.behavior: For this fragment, the built-in parser ignores the dangling closing paragraph tag and does not add an html or body shell.

parsers.label: lxml
parsers.behavior: For this fragment, lxml ignores the dangling closing paragraph tag and wraps the anchor in html and body elements.

parsers.label: html5lib
parsers.behavior: For this fragment, html5lib applies HTML5 recovery rules, adds the document shell, and pairs the dangling closing paragraph with an opening paragraph inside the anchor.

contracts.label: Find anchor content
contracts.detail: Only the presence of the anchor matters for this sample.
contracts.success: All three recovered trees retain an anchor, so this narrow extraction does not depend on their structural differences.
contracts.failure: The selected parser removed the anchor required by the extraction contract.

contracts.label: Require html and body
contracts.detail: Downstream code navigates from a complete document shell.
contracts.success: For this malformed fragment, the selected parser creates the html and body nodes that downstream navigation expects.
contracts.failure: For this fragment, html.parser leaves the anchor at the top level, so code that assumes soup.html.body exists will fail.

contracts.label: Mirror HTML5 recovery
contracts.detail: Tests expect the browser-style repaired paragraph structure.
contracts.success: html5lib applies HTML5 parsing rules and produces the repaired paragraph structure expected by this test contract.
contracts.failure: The selected parser produces a legitimate but different tree. Pin html5lib when browser-like recovery is part of the contract.
